parole.significato: dated or formal, scientific of αγαπόρνιθα (agapórnitha)
lane, back street, side street (small and narrow street or alley)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Katharevousa ἀγυιά (agyiá) from Ancient Greek ἀγυιᾱ́ (aguiā́), less common variant of ἄγυια (águia). Loaned in the 19th century to substitute the Demotic σοκάκι (sokáki) which was a Turkish loanword.
Learned borrowing from Katharevousa ἀγυιόπαις (agyiópais) coinage, from αγυιά (agyiá, “alley”) + παιδ- (paid-, “child”). Compare γυμνασιόπαιδο (gymnasiópaido).
Learned borrowing from Katharevousa ἀερολιμήν (aerolimín) with Standard Modern Greek αερο- (aero-, “air-”) + λιμένας (liménas, “port”) < λιμήν (limḗn). Calque of French aéroport.
Borrowed from Katharevousa αποσύνδεσις (aposýndesis). By surface analysis, αποσυνδέ(ω) (aposyndé(o)) + -ση (-si).

Learned borrowing from Katharevousa ἀποχωρητήριον (apochoritírion) (first attested in 1888), from the past stem αποχωρη- (apochori-) of αποχωρώ (apochoró, “to withdraw, pull out”) + -τήριο (-tírio, “place suffix”).

Learned borrowing from Katharevousa ἀστεροσκοπ(εῖον), since 1848 + modern suffix -είο (-eío). See the Hellenistic ἀστεροσκόπος (asteroskópos, “astronomer; astrologer”). By surface analysis, αστέρ(ας) (astér(as)) + -ο- + -σκοπείο (-skopeío). See, form Modern Greek αστέρι n (astéri, “star”) and σκοπός
Learned borrowing from Katharevousa εἰς (eis), from Ancient Greek εἰς (eis). Doublet of σε (se).
From Katharevousa ἐν γένει (en génei), formed from Ancient Greek ἐν (en) + γένει (génei), dative singular of γένος (génos).
From Katharevousa, formed from Ancient Greek ἐν (en) + συνεχείᾳ (sunekheíāi), dative singular of συνέχεια (sunékheia).
Learned borrowing from Katharevousa σημειωματάριον (simeiomatárion). By surface analysis, σημείωμα (simeíoma, “note”) + -άριο (-ário).

Learned borrowing from Katharevousa ταχυδρομεῖον (tachydromeíon). By surface analysis, ταχυδρόμος (tachydrómos, “postman”) + -είο (-eío), the former from ταχυ- (tachy-, “fast”) + δρόμος (drómos, “road, street”).

Learned borrowing from Katharevousa τοπωνύμι(ον) created in analogy to Koine Greek ἐπωνύμιον (epōnúmion, “surname”) + -ο (Standard Modern Greek neuter suffix). Compound of τοπ- (τόπος) (top- (tópos), “place”) + -ωνύμιο (-onýmio, “-onym”).

parole.significato: ripening, maturing and see senses at verb ωριμάζω (orimázo)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Katharevousa ὡρίμανσις (orímansis), already attested in 1881 and proscribed by Koumanoudis with ironic comments, (also at other dictionaries) because of its formation from nonexistent verb *ὡριμαίνω, instead of the expected form ὡρίμασις (orímasis) (attested since 1796) -moder
